description: Valid binary plist with the last twelve bytes of its 32-byte trailer cut off
notes: The trailer is the last 32 bytes of the file, so truncating a binary plist does not shorten the trailer - it makes the reader parse 32 bytes of object data as one. The offset and reference sizes it finds there are nonsense, which is why the error is ErrorKind::Malformed and not UnexpectedEof. Worth pinning: a positional trailer means truncation is not an EOF condition, and a reader that only checks lengths will happily read garbage as structure.
